title: Genomic Forecasts of Maladaptation in Lycaeides Butterflies
content:
ABSTRACT

Genomic forecasting approaches based on genotype-environment associations (GEAs) are increasingly used to estimate genomic offsets (GOs), which are intended to predict population maladaptation and extinction risk under current or future climatic conditions. Despite their widespread use, only a subset of studies has evaluated how accurately GOs predict maladaptation, limiting their interpretation and application in policy and management. Here, we used GEA analyses to estimate GOs for past, present, and future climates in Lycaeides butterflies, focusing on variation in GOs among populations and their relationships with demographic parameters inferred from population genomic data. Using an RDA-equivalent multivariate linear regression and genotyping-by-sequencing data from 42 Lycaeides populations (922 butterflies), we found that mean annual temperature, cumulative annual precipitation, and hybridization history together explained 47.6% of variation in genome-wide allele frequencies. Genomic offsets differed substantially among populations and across past, present, and future climates, with GOs generally increasing under more distant future climate scenarios. We found no relationship between GOs for present climates and contemporary effective population size. In contrast, genetic diversity, which reflects long-term effective population size, and local rates of gene flow together explained 27.3% of variation in contemporary GOs. Populations with higher genetic diversity and more gene flow exhibited lower GOs, consistent both with stronger drift increasing genomic mismatch in low-diversity populations and with the hypothesis that genetic diversity enhances adaptive capacity and that gene flow may introduce adaptive alleles. While these results show that GOs covary with genomic estimates of genetic diversity and connectivity, we caution against simplistic interpretations of GOs as direct measures of maladaptation in conservation and management contexts.
